properties.statement:
`constrains` AND `governed_by` REFUSE A `note` THEIR OWN EDGE TYPES DECLARE. Reported by dev_storyflow 2026-08-23, re-verified live by them while writing the entry rather than recalled, and CONFIRMED against reflow2 0.47.1 on 2026-09-04 by reading the request structs.

THEIR EVIDENCE:
  constrains(..., note=...) → unknown field `note`, expected one of `constraint_id`, `target_type`, `target_id`, `contribution`, `basis`, `measured_at`
  governed_by(..., note=...) → unknown field `note`, expected one of `from_type`, `from_id`, `to_type`, `to_id`, `ruling`
And in the same session `describe_schema(from=DesignRule, to=Project)` lists CONSTRAINS' properties as basis, contribution, measured_at, NOTE — and GOVERNED_BY's as NOTE, ruling.

CONFIRMED 2026-09-04: `ConstrainsReq` at crates/reflow2-mcp/src/service.rs:1979 and `GovernedByReq` at :2208 — neither struct declares `note`. The schema declares the field, the typed constructor cannot reach it, and the error names a SHORTER allowlist without hinting a longer one exists.

WHAT IT COSTS, in their words: the note is the part a later reader actually needs — WHY this rule binds this project, WHY this requirement is governed by that decision. They wanted it twice in one day and both times fell back to `create_edge` with a raw props object, which works but abandons the typed constructor's validation FOR THE WHOLE CALL. An agent less inclined to run `describe_schema` would simply drop the note and lose the reasoning.

⭐ THEY NAME THE CLASS, AND IT IS ALREADY ON THIS PROJECT'S RECORD: two surfaces of one system disagreeing about what is writable, with THE MORE CONVENIENT SURFACE OFFERING LESS. Same shape as the revise-design-vs-create_node disagreement the served skill already records, and adjacent to `fact:a-third-of-declared-properties-name-nothing-any-tool-accepts` and `req:declared-vocabulary-is-reachable-from-the-surface` — which is ACCEPTED, so this is an unbuilt half of accepted intent rather than a new want.

⭐ THE PATTERN THEY POINT AT FOR THE FIX IS ALREADY BUILT ELSEWHERE: `create_node`'s `undeclared` block, which they praise in the same entry for teaching them that a DesignRule's fields are `category` and `enforced` rather than the three they guessed. Accept the field, and say what you did not recognise.

ADJACENT, FROM THE SAME ENTRY AND NOT CLAIMED HERE: there is no `add_design_rule`, so a DesignRule is writable only through generic `create_node`, and its field names are discoverable only by `describe_schema`.
